chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who bows (ruku') then raises his head: does he begin by placing his hands on the ground or on his knees? He said, 'It does not harm him whichever of those he begins with; his prayer is accepted from him.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: His saying (peace be upon him) 'It does not harm him whichever of those he begins with' means that his prayer is not invalidated, although the preferable method is what we have mentioned earlier, that he should meet the ground with his hands, except in case of necessity.

key_terms.يَتَلَقَّى الْأَرْضَ بِيَدَيْهِ: meet the ground with his hands

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on placing hands on the ground versus knees when rising from bowing in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of rising from ruku', establishing that the sequence of placing hands on the ground versus the knees does not invalidate the prayer, reflecting the Shia principle of flexibility in sunnah actions. Shaykh al-Tusi’s commentary highlights that while placing hands on the ground first is the preferred (afdhal) method, the permissibility of the alternative acknowledges practical necessities, ensuring the worshipper's confidence in their ritual validity.
